newsitem.title: USA: Burlington says weather hurt Q1 profits.
newsitem.headline: Burlington says weather hurt Q1 profits.

text.p: Burlington Northern Santa Fe Corp on Tuesday said severe weather this winter may have cut revenues by about $100 million and increased expenses by some $50 million.

"Severe weather conditions have affected operations throughout the northern plains and the Pacific Northwest since the beginning of the year," said Robert Krebs, Burlington's chairman, president and chief executive.
Earlier, Burlington reported first quarter 1997 net income of $0.95 per share on revenues of $2.036 billion compared with $1.21 a share on revenues of $2.027 billion last year.
First Call said analysts forecast earnings of $0.98 per share.

Krebs said the weather had a hand in recurring and protracted outages on many parts of the system, the cost of repairing track, signals and equipment and other operating inefficiencies. He also noted some carryover effect will be felt in the second quarter because of an April blizzard in the Powder River Basin, which shut down coal operations for two days and by flooding in the upper Midwest.

Burlington said it incurred a $48 million, or 14 percent decline, in agricultural commodities revenues due primarily to weather-related service problems affecting shipments of wheat, corn and soybeans and a poor hard, red winter wheat crop.
First quarter 1997 operating expenses were $1.71 billion, $65 million above 1996, Burlington said.
